title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الثانى- تابع
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape two, continued
body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد الله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين أما بعد فقد كان الحديث في الحلقة الماضية توقف عند هم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأمر، وهم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالأمر ينقسم إلى قسمين، إلى هم عقبه الترك، أي إلى أن يهم بأمر يقدر عليه فيتركه، أي أن يكون أراد أن يفعل فعلا ثم قوي لديه تركه فتركه كهمه بتحريق بيوت المتخلفين عن الصلاة، وإلى هم حال دونه مانع كصيام اليوم التاسع من شهر المحرم، فإنه قال: [لئن بقيت إلى قابل لأصومن التاسع]، فتوفاه الله ونقله إلى الرفيق الأعلى قبل أن ينفذ عزمه، فالهم إذن إذا كان تركه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من غير مانع كهمه بتحريق بيوت المخالفين عن الصلاة فهذا النوع من الهم لا يقتدى به لأنه لم يفعله..
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

To proceed: the discussion in the last session stopped at the Prophet's resolving upon a matter, upon whom be God's blessing and peace. The Prophet's resolving upon a matter, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, divides into two kinds. There is a resolve followed by abandonment — that is, that he resolves upon a matter he is able to do and then leaves it; that is, that he intended to do an act and then leaving it prevailed with him, so he left it, as with his resolving to burn the houses of those who stayed away from the prayer. And there is a resolve which an impediment prevented, as with fasting the ninth day of the month of Muharram, for he said: "If I remain until next year, I shall certainly fast the ninth." Then God took him and removed him to the Highest Companion before he could carry out his resolve. So the resolve, then: where the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, left it with no impediment — as with his resolving to burn the houses of those who differed concerning the prayer — this kind of resolve is not to be taken as a precedent to follow, because he did not do it..

flags.context: the second mention of the same example; the first mention reads المتخلفين عن الصلاة
options: those who differed concerning the prayer
those who stayed away from the prayer [reading al-mutakhallifīn, as in the first mention]
those who opposed [the Prophet] over the prayer
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. The Sheikh gives the same example twice in three lines. The first time the word is al-mutakhallifīn, 'those who stay away'; the second time it is al-mukhālifīn, 'those who differ or oppose'. The two are close in writing and the second is almost certainly a transcription slip for the first, since the hadith concerns non-attendance, and since al-mukhālifīn does not take the preposition ʿan. The style guide forbids silently repairing a source defect, so body_en renders each occurrence as printed and the discrepancy is recorded here. A reviewer working from the audio can settle it in a moment.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

'Resolve' renders hamm — the Prophet's forming an intention to act. The classification of his resolves is a point of legal theory: whether an act he intended but did not perform establishes a precedent. The reasoning has been kept as a chain rather than compressed to its conclusion.
'The Highest Companion' renders al-rafīq al-aʿlā, from the Prophet's last words; it is an idiom for his death and has not been paraphrased.

The source's opening doxology reads al-ḥamd Allāh where the standard form is al-ḥamdu li-llāh. The slip is in the source and body_ar preserves it; it carries no difference of meaning and has not been separately flagged.
The source encloses the hadith in square brackets rather than the angle quotation marks it uses elsewhere. The variation is the source's and has no significance for the text.
